1: Make a graph with this code!
```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, hp, color = as.factor(gear)))+ geom_point() + scale_fill_manual(values = c("chocolate", "saddlebrown", "darkorange")) + themes_classic() + labs(x = "Meters per Gallon", y = "Horsepower", legend = "Gear")

```

2: Open the starwars dataset, check the class of the character name data, and then turn it into a factor.
```{r}
data(starwars)
class(starwars$character)
starwarsNames<- as.factor(starwars$character)
```


3: Create and save a function that divides all numbers in a column by 10. Test it on the starwars mass column.
```{r}
divByTen<- function(number){number/10}
starwars$mass<- divByTen
```


Code Solutions:
1:
```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, hp, color = as.factor(gear)))+ geom_point() + scale_color_manual(values = c("chocolate", "saddlebrown", "darkorange")) + theme_classic() + labs(x = "Miles per Gallon", y = "Horsepower", color = "Gear")
```

2:
```{r}
data(starwars)
class(starwars$name)
starwarsNames<- as.factor(starwars$name)
```

3:
```{r}
divByTen<- function(number){number/10}
divByTen(starwars$mass)
```
